title: Affordable housing retrofits and special events and arts plans
subtitle: Live streaming policy, dog and sign by-law fixes, HR policy updates, pumping station funding and election-period spending authority
overview: The Community and Infrastructure Services Committee recommended funding for a pilot to retrofit affordable housing. It backed a one-time $100,000 contribution in 2026 to Kitchener Housing Incorporated and a $50,000 founding member contribution in 2027 to the Retrofit Affordable Housing Waterloo Region program {{vote:m7}}.

The committee also recommended two four-year action plans for 2027-2030, one for special events {{vote:m8}} and one for arts and creative industries {{vote:m9}}. Both guide how staff evaluate opportunities within existing mandates and resources. Any changes to service levels, staffing or budgets must come back to Council through issue papers and the annual budget process.

Six routine items were passed together in one consent vote. They included by-law housekeeping amendments, a live streaming policy for sports and recreation, updates to the affordable housing incentive policy, $290,000 for added work at the Carson Drive Sewage Pumping Station, modernized HR policies, and temporary spending authority for the Chief Administrative Officer during the pre-election period. All of these are recommendations that Council must still adopt.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a one-time $100,000 contribution to Kitchener Housing Incorporated in 2026 and a $50,000 founding member contribution in 2027 to the Retrofit Affordable Housing Waterloo Region pilot {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended approving the plan as the guiding framework for special events and directing staff to produce an abbreviated version for stakeholders, sponsors and residents {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Arts and Creative Industries Action Plan
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse the 2027-2030 plan as the framework for clarifying the City's role and prioritizing arts and creative industries work {{vote:m9}}.

The committee recommended that, if the provincial restricted acts provisions take effect between Nomination Day and the end of the term, the Chief Administrative Officer may approve unbudgeted spending over $50,000, with approvals reported to Council afterward.
The committee recommended allocating an additional $290,000 from the Sanitary Capital Reserve for design, contract administration and construction of additional works.
The committee recommended amending Council Policy FIN-GRA-2038 for not-for-profit affordable rental and co-op housing incentives, using the revised policy in the staff report.
The committee recommended approving a policy on live streaming of sports and recreation activities and authorizing staff to manage related procedures and agreements.
The committee recommended housekeeping amendments covering dog, sign, tree, fireworks and boulevard beautification rules, plus a by-law amending the Boulevard Beautification chapter.
